maya: Ran the nightly perf suite on the int8 paged-attention branch, and we have a ~22% tail latency regression for seq=1024, batch=4 compared to main. not a small blip.
jon: ugh, is that on fused kernels or falling back to the reference kernel?
maya: looks like the kernel selector picks `flash_hybrid_fallback` for that combo. earlier it picked `fused_flash_v2` on main.
li: any signs of KV layout contributing? we've had subtle alignment issues for interleaved layouts with int8.
maya: that's the thing — when we force `kv_layout=separate` the regression disappears (within noise). interleaved shows the hit.
sam: can you paste the perf summary + the kernel selection log?
maya: sure — snippet below from the run log:
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:02Z] model=rf-7b-int8 seq=1024 bsz=4 kernel=flash_hybrid_fallback tokens/ms=8.3 p95=142ms p99=198ms
[2026-03-17T02:14:03Z] selector: tried fused_flash_v2 -> rejected (stride_misaligned)
[2026-03-17T02:14:03Z] selector: fallback-> flash_hybrid_fallback
```
jon: `stride_misaligned` is new; what check triggers that? I thought we only check dtype+seq+sm architecture.
li: we added an alignment safety check last month: if kv stride % 64 != 0 and dtype!=fp16 we avoid fused kernels to prevent bank conflicts on Ampere. maybe it's too conservative for int8-packed layouts.
maya: profiling shows a high number of L2 load stalls and warp serialization on the interleaved layout. flamegraph attached in the job (perf-bot).
perf-bot: quick report: run=2012345678-rt-nightly, flamegraph_url=https://ci.internal/runs/2012345678/flame.svg, membank_conflicts=high, kernel_calls: fused_flash_v2=0 fused_flash_v1=0 flash_hybrid_fallback=78

sam: interesting that separate layout avoids it. do we know if interleaved layout adds extra padding so stride becomes odd?
li: interleaved packs kv per head: stride = head_size * dtype_size * heads + pad. For int8 we pack 4 bytes per 4 elements into a byte, stride math can produce non-64 multiples if pad calculation changed.

jon: hypothesis: our quantize packing changed in the int8 path (new packer) so the computed stride lost the previous rounding-to-64. selector now flags misaligned and we fallback. fallback kernel is slower for large seqs.
maya: test: patched packer to round stride up to 64 and re-ran quick smoke — kernel selector now picks fused_flash_v2 and p95 drops back to baseline.
sam: can we do a safer change? maybe loosen the stride check to allow 32 alignment on Ampere when dtype=int8 and head_size%32==0?
li: safe plan: 1) add a diagnostic flag to `selector_debug` that prints computed stride, pad, and alignment check; 2) run CI perf comparing packer-old vs packer-new and layout variations (interleaved/separate); 3) add a microbenchmark for fused kernel with intentionally misaligned stride to reproduce bank-conflict pattern.
maya: I started the CI matrix: packer-{old,new} x kv-{interleaved,separate} x seq={512,1024,2048} x bsz={1,4}. will share links.

perf-bot: matrix started: 2012345678-ci-matrix, jobs=12, est_complete=20m

jon: also think we should update kernel selector to prefer fused variant if simulated memory coalescing metric is acceptable even with stride!=64. currently it's a boolean check; convert to a score and compare expected throughput.
sam: yeah, a score-based decision will let us recover good cases and still avoid pathological ones. add telemetry to record when selector chooses fallback because of alignment so we can tune thresholds.
li: agreed. i'll make a small PR: change `alignment_gate` boolean -> `alignment_score` float in kernel selector, add telemetry tag `alignment_score=<float>` when logging selection.
maya: perfect. after the packer fix + selector tuning smoke I can run full nightly to confirm no regressions for other seqs.

jon: thanks team — nice catch. small ask: add a unit test that constructs an int8 interleaved tensor with varying pad to verify selector behavior deterministically.
li: on it.

sam: marking follow-ups: PRs from li (selector telemetry), li (unit test), maya (packer stride rounding), ops (CI diff results). i'll file tickets. :white_check_mark:

maya: filing ticket now and will drop links here when CI completes.

perf-bot: ci-complete: 2012345678-ci-matrix, results_url=https://ci.internal/runs/2012345678/matrix.html, summary=pack-new + round-up -> fused chosen for seq=1024/bsz=4, p95 restored
jon: nice. once PRs land let's schedule a canary deploy to dedicated cluster and monitor token/ms and membank_conflicts for a day.
maya: will do. thanks all :rocket:
